Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this 3-year-old girl, whom I have followed since early infancy when developmental and physical concerns first came to light. 

She lives at home with her parents and two older siblings, all of whom are healthy. Family history is non-contributory, with no parental consanguinity. Her immunizations are current, and she takes only an over-the-counter multivitamin. Notably, there has been no history of seizures, tremors, or unprovoked staring episodes to date.

On physical exam, her vital signs are stable, and cardiovascular and respiratory evaluations are completely normal. Neurologically, she exhibits marked generalized low muscle tone and significantly diminished deep tendon reflexes across all extremities. Craniofacial inspection reveals prominent coarsening of her facial contours, a distinctly flattened nasal root, and noticeable bitemporal constriction giving a tapered appearance to her upper face. A formal auditory evaluation previously confirmed bilateral sensorineural deficits. Furthermore, her abdomen is soft and non-tender, but organomegaly is prominent; the liver edge extends approximately 3.5 cm below the right costal margin, and the spleen tip is readily palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin.

Given the constellation of these persistent findings since her first year of life, I would value your expert assessment and recommendations regarding an appropriate diagnostic evaluation.

Sincerely,
Dr. Evelyn Vance
General Pediatrics
